# 1 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 2

---

## Council Notes

**On "his kidneys trembled" (v.24):** EMET preserves the anatomical idiom (*enetinachthesan hoi nephrol autou* — "his kidneys shook"). LOGOS renders it "his heart was stirred." PNEUMA: "burned in his gut." The kidneys as the seat of deep emotion is a Hebrew idiom that survives into the Greek. A middle path: "he was moved to his very depths" preserves the visceral nature without the puzzling anatomical specificity.

**On Phinehas allusion (v.26):** All translators recognize and preserve this as a deliberate echo of Numbers 25. It is the theological key to the entire chapter — Mattathias presents himself as a new Phinehas, and Judas will be commissioned as a new Joshua.

**On "the Hasideans" (v.42):** All translators preserve "Hasideans" as a proper group name. This is correct — the *Asidaioi* are the precursors of the Pharisaic movement.

**On the deathbed speech (vv.49-68):** This is one of the most important passages in the Deuterocanon. The roll call of faithful ancestors (Abraham, Joseph, Phinehas, Joshua, Caleb, David, Elijah, Hananiah/Azariah/Mishael, Daniel) is a theological manifesto. The speech should maintain its rhetorical force without over-dramatizing.

---

1. In those days Mattathias son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
2. He had five sons: John, called Gaddi;
3. Simon, called Thassi;
4. Judas, who was called Maccabeus;
5. Eleazar, called Avaran; and Jonathan, called Apphus.
6. When he saw the blasphemies being committed in Judah and in Jerusalem,
7. he said: "Woe is me! Why was I born to see this — the ruin of my people and the destruction of the holy city — and to sit by while she is given into the hand of enemies and the sanctuary into the hand of strangers?
8. Her temple has become like a man stripped of honor.
9. The precious vessels of her glory have been carried into exile; her infants have been killed in her streets, her young men by the sword of the enemy.
10. What nation has not taken its portion of her palaces and seized her spoils?
11. All her adornment has been stripped away. Once free, she has become a slave.
12. And see — our holy things, our beauty, our glory have been laid waste, and the Gentiles have defiled them.
13. Why then should we live any longer?"
14. Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, put on sackcloth, and mourned greatly.
15. The king's officers who were enforcing the apostasy came to the town of Modein to make the people sacrifice.
16. Many from Israel came to them, and Mattathias and his sons gathered with them.
17. The king's officers said to Mattathias: "You are a leader, a distinguished and great man in this city, supported by sons and brothers.
18. Come, be the first to carry out the king's command, as all the nations have done and the people of Judah and those who remain in Jerusalem; and you and your household will be among the friends of the king, and you and your sons will be honored with silver and gold and many gifts."
19. Mattathias answered in a loud voice: "Even if every nation within the king's dominion obeys him, and every man forsakes the worship of his fathers and chooses to follow his commands,
20. yet I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
21. Heaven forbid that we should forsake the Torah and its ordinances.
22. We will not obey the king's words, turning aside from our worship to the right or to the left."
23. When he had finished speaking, a man of Israel came forward in the sight of all and sacrificed upon the altar in Modein, in compliance with the king's command.
24. When Mattathias saw it, he was moved to his very depths with burning zeal; in righteous indignation he ran forward and slaughtered the man upon the altar.
25. At the same time he killed the king's officer who was compelling them to sacrifice, and he tore down the altar.
26. He acted with zeal for the Torah, just as Phinehas had done to Zimri son of Salu.
27. Then Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice: "Let everyone who is zealous for the Torah and who stands by the covenant follow me!"
28. He and his sons fled to the hills and left behind all they had in the city.
29. Then many who were seeking righteousness and justice went down to the wilderness to dwell there —
30. they and their sons and their wives and their livestock — because evil had pressed so heavily upon them.
31. Word was brought to the king's officers and the forces in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had rejected the king's command had gone down to the hiding places in the wilderness.
32. Many went in pursuit and overtook them; they encamped against them and prepared to attack on the sabbath day.
33. They called to them: "Come out now, do as the king commands, and you will live."
34. They replied: "We will not come out, and we will not do the king's command to profane the sabbath day."
35. The enemy hastened to attack them.
36. But the men offered no resistance. They threw no stones, blocked no entrances,
37. but said: "Let us all die with a clear conscience. Heaven and earth are witnesses against you that you are killing us unjustly."
38. The attack came on the sabbath day, and they died — men, wives, children, and livestock — about a thousand souls.
39. When Mattathias and his friends heard this, they mourned deeply for them.
40. And each said to his neighbor: "If we all do as our brothers did and refuse to fight the Gentiles for our lives and our ordinances, they will soon destroy us from the earth."
41. On that day they reached this decision: "If anyone attacks us on the sabbath day, we will fight him, so that we do not all die as our brothers died in the hiding places."
42. Then a company of the Hasideans joined them — mighty men of Israel, every one who had given himself willingly to the Torah.
43. And all who were fleeing from the evils joined them and reinforced them.
44. They organized an army and struck down sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath; the survivors fled to the Gentiles.
45. Mattathias and his friends went through the region tearing down the pagan altars.
46. They forcibly circumcised all uncircumcised boys they found within the borders of Israel.
47. They drove the arrogant before them, and the work went forward in their hands.
48. They rescued the Torah from the hands of the Gentiles and the kings, and they never let the sinner gain the upper hand.
49. When the days of Mattathias drew near for him to die, he said to his sons: "Now arrogance and contempt have grown strong; it is a time of ruin and furious anger.
50. My sons, be zealous for the Torah and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
51. Remember the deeds of the ancestors in their generations, and you will receive great honor and an everlasting name.
52. Was not Abraham found faithful under trial, and was it not counted to him as righteousness?
53. Joseph in his time of distress kept the commandment, and became lord of Egypt.
54. Phinehas our father, for his burning zeal, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
55. Joshua, because he fulfilled his commission, became a judge in Israel.
56. Caleb, because he gave his honest testimony in the assembly, received an inheritance in the land.
57. David, because he was compassionate, inherited the throne of the kingdom forever.
58. Elijah, for his burning zeal for the Torah, was taken up into heaven.
59. Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael believed, and were saved from the flame.
60. Daniel, because of his integrity, was delivered from the mouth of the lions.
61. Consider this, generation by generation: none who put their trust in him will want for strength.
62. Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory will turn to dung and worms.
63. Today he is exalted, and tomorrow he is nowhere to be found, for he has returned to his dust and his scheming has come to nothing.
64. My sons, be courageous and strong in the Torah, for through it you will be glorified.
65. Here is your brother Simon — I know him to be a man of wise counsel. Listen to him all your days; he shall be a father to you.
66. And Judas Maccabeus, who has been strong and mighty from his youth — let him be your commander and lead the campaign of the people.
67. Gather to yourselves all who observe the Torah, and exact the vengeance of your people.
68. Repay the Gentiles in full, and hold fast to the commandment of the Torah."
69. Then he blessed them and was gathered to his ancestors.
70. He died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year, and his sons buried him in the tomb of his fathers at Modein, and all Israel made great lamentation over him.
